advances:
The endpoint first-moment coefficient cannot collapse in a compact
genuine-fan gauge.  There is a canonical pair of points, one in each
midpoint body from
\(P_\varnothing\times Q_1\) and
\(P_\varnothing\times Q_2\), whose transverse separation \(B_U\)
satisfies
\[
C B_U^2+A B_U>\frac15.
\]
Here \(A,C>0\) depend only on the compact-gauge diameter and the
normalized genuine-fan gradients.  Hence \(B_U\) has an explicit
positive zeroth-order modulus.

The proof uses the first and second crossings through the canonical
left tails.  The third crossing and the sum of all three crossings
then supply the exact scalar closure.  In particular, forced emptiness
of \(Q_\varnothing\) and \(R_\varnothing\) gives
\[
k\leq2M-1,
\]
which replaces any use of a no-half inequality.

The endpoint offset condition alone also gives
\[
\liminf_{d\downarrow0}\frac{B_U(d)}d
\geq\frac6{H_0}.
\]
Under the full crossing and tail hypotheses, the stronger positive
zeroth-order modulus shows that an expansion
\(B_U(d)=\beta_Ud+o(d)\) cannot occur.  Thus, once a separate
finite-stage estimate
\(\Delta_3\geq cB_U-Ed\) is proved, the exact third crossing
\(\Delta_3=0\) is contradicted for all sufficiently small \(d\).
This packet supplies the endpoint first-moment half of that argument.

proof:
The normalization (5) gives an exact parameterization of the paired
endpoint cuts.  Set
\[
a_i=3d\left(L_i+\frac13\right),
\qquad
b_i=3d\left(\frac13-L_i\right)=2d-a_i.
\tag{17}
\]
Then
\[
P_J
=A_0\cap
\{\psi_i\leq a_i\ (i\in J),\
  \psi_i>a_i\ (i\notin J)\},
\]
\[
Q_J
=A_2\cap
\{\psi_i\leq b_i\ (i\in J),\
  \psi_i>b_i\ (i\notin J)\}.
\tag{18}
\]
The offset hypothesis in accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f` gives
\[
\sum_i a_i=3d\left(\sum_iL_i+1\right)<0.
\tag{19}
\]
Consequently, if
\[
\delta=-\sum_i a_i,\qquad
\eta=\sum_i b_i,
\]
then
\[
\delta>0,\qquad
\eta=6d+\delta>6d.
\tag{20}
\]

We first estimate the transverse first moments of \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\).
For \(y\in Q_1\), write
\[
\alpha=b_1-\psi_1(y)\geq0,\qquad
\sigma=\psi_2(y)-b_2>0.
\]
Using (6),
\[
\psi_3(y)-b_3
=\alpha-\sigma-\eta>0.
\]
Hence
\[
\alpha>\eta+\sigma
\]
and
\[
(\psi_1-\psi_2)(y)
=b_1-b_2-\alpha-\sigma
<b_1-b_2-\eta-2\sigma.
\tag{21}
\]

Similarly, for \(y\in Q_2\), write
\[
\rho=\psi_1(y)-b_1>0,\qquad
\gamma=b_2-\psi_2(y)\geq0.
\]
The inequality \(\psi_3(y)>b_3\) gives
\[
\gamma>\eta+\rho
\]
and therefore
\[
(\psi_1-\psi_2)(y)
>b_1-b_2+\eta+2\rho.
\tag{22}
\]

Let
\[
\overline\sigma
=\frac1{q_1}\int_{Q_1}(\psi_2-b_2),
\qquad
\overline\rho
=\frac1{q_2}\int_{Q_2}(\psi_1-b_1).
\tag{23}
\]
Averaging (21)-(22), using (9), and cancelling the common
\(x_\varnothing\) term gives
\[
B_U>
\frac{\eta+\overline\sigma+\overline\rho}{H}.
\tag{24}
\]

The two mean slacks have exact area lower bounds.  Slice \(Q_1\) by
the signed-distance coordinate
\[
r=\frac{\psi_2-b_2}{\|\nabla\psi_2\|}>0.
\]
Every section has length at most \(D\).  Among all nonnegative section
length functions bounded by \(D\) and having integral \(q_1\), the
first moment is minimized by filling
\([0,q_1/D]\) with density \(D\).  Therefore
\[
\int_{Q_1}(\psi_2-b_2)
\geq
\|\nabla\psi_2\|\frac{q_1^2}{2D},
\]
so
\[
\overline\sigma
\geq
\frac{\|\nabla\psi_2\|q_1}{2D}.
\tag{25}
\]
The same argument gives
\[
\overline\rho
\geq
\frac{\|\nabla\psi_1\|q_2}{2D}.
\tag{26}
\]
Combining (24)-(26) yields
\[
B_U>
\frac{\eta+g(q_1+q_2)/(2D)}H.
\tag{27}
\]
In particular,
\[
\eta<H B_U,
\qquad
q_1+q_2<\frac{2DH}{g}B_U=A B_U.
\tag{28}
\]
Equations (20), (24), and (28) prove \(B_U>0\) and give
\[
B_U>\frac{6d}{H}.
\tag{29}
\]
Passing to (15) proves (16).

We next bound the empty endpoint cell.  The affine map
\[
y\longmapsto(\psi_1(y),\psi_2(y))
\]
has Jacobian magnitude \(J_\psi\).  By (6), the three strict
inequalities defining \(P_\varnothing\) place it inside
\[
\{\psi_1>a_1,\ \psi_2>a_2,\
  \psi_1+\psi_2<-a_3\}.
\]
In the \((\psi_1,\psi_2)\)-plane this is a right triangle with both
legs equal to
\(\delta=-a_1-a_2-a_3\).  Therefore
\[
p_\varnothing
\leq\frac{\delta^2}{2J_\psi}
<\frac{\eta^2}{2J_\psi}
<\frac{H^2}{2J_\psi}B_U^2
=C B_U^2.
\tag{30}
\]

It remains to use the crossings and tails.  From the support (2),
\[
v_1=1-q_2,\qquad
v_2=1-q_1,\qquad
v_3=q_{123}.
\tag{31}
\]
Subtracting the crossing in (4) from its left-tail inequality gives
\[
u_i+v_i\leq1.
\tag{32}
\]
Equations (31)-(32) imply
\[
u_1\leq q_2,\qquad
u_2\leq q_1.
\tag{33}
\]

Every \(P\)-cell other than
\(P_\varnothing\) and \(P_3\) has index \(1\) or \(2\).  Hence
\[
M-p_\varnothing-p_3\leq u_1+u_2.
\tag{34}
\]
Also
\[
p_3\leq u_3\leq1-v_3\leq1
\tag{35}
\]
by (32).  Put
\[
\varepsilon=p_\varnothing+q_1+q_2.
\tag{36}
\]
Equations (33)-(35) give
\[
M\leq1+\varepsilon.
\tag{37}
\]
The third crossing and (34) give
\[
h=u_3+v_3+c_3
\geq u_3
\geq p_3
\geq M-\varepsilon
\geq1-\varepsilon.
\tag{38}
\]

We now sum the three crossings.  Accepted fact
`0e51a47a9add571f` forces
\[
Q_\varnothing=R_\varnothing=\varnothing.
\]
Since the exact cells partition \(A_2\) and \(K\), this gives
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3v_i
=\sum_{J\ne\varnothing}|J|q_J\geq1,
\]
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3c_i
=\sum_{J\ne\varnothing}|J|r_J\geq k.
\tag{39}
\]
Because \(\sum_i u_i\geq0\), summing (4) and using (39) gives
\[
\frac{2(M+1+k)}3=3h
=\sum_i u_i+\sum_i v_i+\sum_i c_i
\geq1+k.
\]
Therefore
\[
k\leq2M-1.
\tag{40}
\]
Using (37) in (40),
\[
h=\frac{2(M+1+k)}9
\leq\frac{2M}{3}
\leq\frac23+\frac{2\varepsilon}{3}.
\tag{41}
\]
Combining (38) and (41) gives
\[
1-\varepsilon
\leq\frac23+\frac{2\varepsilon}{3},
\]
and hence
\[
\boxed{\qquad
\varepsilon\geq\frac15.
\qquad}
\tag{42}
\]

Finally, (28), (30), and (36) give the strict estimate
\[
\varepsilon
<C B_U^2+A B_U.
\tag{43}
\]
Combining (42)-(43) proves (12), and solving the positive quadratic
inequality proves (13).

For completeness, on any fixed low-vertex polygonal stratum the
first-order cap equations are explicit.  If the three bodies and the
normalized affine functions are fixed to first order, put
\[
\ell_{0i}
=\frac{\mathcal H^1(A_0\cap\{\psi_i=a_i\})}
       {\|\nabla\psi_i\|},
\quad
\ell_{2i}
=\frac{\mathcal H^1(A_2\cap\{\psi_i=b_i\})}
       {\|\nabla\psi_i\|},
\]
\[
\ell_{Ki}
=\frac{\mathcal H^1(K\cap\{\psi_i=d\})}
       {\|\nabla\psi_i\|}.
\tag{44}
\]
Differentiating the three crossings on that stratum gives
\[
(\ell_{0i}-\ell_{2i})a_i'
+2\ell_{2i}+\ell_{Ki}=h'
\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\tag{45}
\]
For fixed total areas, \(h'=0\).  Regardless of how a triangle or
quadrilateral ansatz solves (45), the exact estimates (27)-(43)
remain valid.  Thus no actual low-vertex endpoint realization
satisfying the stated hypotheses can have a finite first-order
coefficient \(\beta_U\) with zero zeroth-order separation.

If, in addition, a finite-stage geometric argument proves
\[
\Delta_3\geq cB_U-Ed
\]
with \(c>0\) and finite \(E\), then (13) gives
\(\Delta_3>0\) for all sufficiently small \(d\), contradicting the
exact third crossing.  This implication uses the displayed stability
estimate as an additional hypothesis; its proof is not part of the
endpoint first-moment lemma.
statement:
Assume the affine sign-plane hypotheses, exact-cell convention, and
midpoint compatibility of accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f`.  Normalize
\[
m=|A_2|=1,\qquad M=|A_0|\geq1.
\tag{1}
\]
Assume
\[
p_\varnothing>0
\]
and that the positive \(Q\)-support is exactly
\[
\{123,1,2,12\}.
\tag{2}
\]
Write
\[
p_J=|P_J|,\qquad q_J=|Q_J|,\qquad r_J=|R_J|,
\]
\[
u_i=\sum_{J\ni i}p_J,\qquad
v_i=\sum_{J\ni i}q_J,\qquad
c_i=\sum_{J\ni i}r_J,
\]
\[
k=|K|,\qquad
h=\frac{2(M+1+k)}9.
\tag{3}
\]
Assume the three crossings and the canonical left tails:
\[
u_i+v_i+c_i=h,\qquad
c_i+1\geq h
\quad(i=1,2,3).
\tag{4}
\]
No no-half inequality is assumed.

Let \(d>0\), and define normalized affine functions
\[
\psi_i=3d\left(f_i+\frac13\right)
\quad(i=1,2,3).
\tag{5}
\]
Then
\[
\psi_1+\psi_2+\psi_3=0.
\tag{6}
\]
Assume their linear parts are pairwise nonparallel.  Put
\[
J_\psi=
\left|\det(\nabla\psi_1,\nabla\psi_2)\right|>0,
\]
\[
g=\min\{\|\nabla\psi_1\|,\|\nabla\psi_2\|\}>0,
\qquad
H=\|\nabla(\psi_1-\psi_2)\|>0,
\tag{7}
\]
and suppose
\[
\operatorname{diam}(A_2)\leq D.
\tag{8}
\]

Let \(x_\varnothing\) be the area centroid of
\(P_\varnothing\), and let \(y_i\) be the area centroid of \(Q_i\)
for \(i=1,2\).  Define
\[
z_i=\frac{x_\varnothing+y_i}{2}
\in
\frac{P_\varnothing+\overline{Q_i}}2
\subseteq K,
\tag{9}
\]
and define the canonical transverse base
\[
B_U=
\frac{(\psi_1-\psi_2)(z_2)
      -(\psi_1-\psi_2)(z_1)}{H}.
\tag{10}
\]
Then \(B_U>0\).  With
\[
A=\frac{2DH}{g},
\qquad
C=\frac{H^2}{2J_\psi},
\tag{11}
\]
one has
\[
\boxed{\qquad
C B_U^2+A B_U>\frac15.
\qquad}
\tag{12}
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\boxed{\qquad
B_U>
\frac{\sqrt{A^2+4C/5}-A}{2C}>0.
\qquad}
\tag{13}
\]

For a compact genuine-fan family, uniform upper bounds for \(D,H\)
and \(J_\psi^{-1}\), together with a uniform positive lower bound for
\(g\), turn (13) into a uniform positive modulus.  In the symmetric
standard fan, where the three gradients have unit length and mutual
angle \(120^\circ\),
\[
g=1,\qquad
H=\sqrt3,\qquad
J_\psi=\frac{\sqrt3}{2},
\]
so (12) becomes
\[
\sqrt3\,B_U^2+2\sqrt3\,D B_U>\frac15.
\tag{14}
\]

Finally, if \(d\downarrow0\), the normalized gradients converge to a
genuine fan, and one assumes
\[
B_U(d)=\beta_Ud+o(d),
\tag{15}
\]
then the endpoint offset condition alone implies
\[
\beta_U\geq\frac6{H_0},
\qquad
H_0=\lim_{d\downarrow0}
\|\nabla(\psi_1-\psi_2)\|.
\tag{16}
\]
Under (1)-(4), (13) shows that (15) cannot occur at all: the
zeroth-order separation is uniformly positive.
